Congratulations to Zach Taylor, YCS Origins Dragon Duel Champion! He used his Kozmo Deck to defeat Eli Buckwalter, and now he’s taking home this Dragon Duel trophy and a set of the Darklord YCS prize cards!
Zach will get his name added to the Hall of Champions!

Day 1 of YCS Origins has come to a close. With eight rounds of Swiss play completed, we’ll have two more before cutting to the Top 32. The Duelists advancing to tomorrow’s portion of the tournament will be the ones with at least 16 points, or the top 128 Duelists (whichever group is larger).
So far, the majority of the field is comprised of a mixture of Kozmo, Monarchs, Burning Abyss, and Performapal Pendulum Decks. The Kozmo Decks are primarily using
. Monarchs seem to mostly be split into two variants. Most of them have been using
, while a smaller number are using no Extra Deck to take advantage of

. Burning Abyss Decks are almost entirely using both Phantom Knights and Speedroids, though a small number eschew the Speedroids. Finally, the Pendulum Decks. Most are similar to the Performapal Dracoslayer builds we’ve seen for a while, but all kinds of variants are popping up, such as ones with Majespecters, Madolche,
, and more. It’s hard to pin down any exact build for the average Pendulum Deck.
Check back in tomorrow for more written coverage right here, or check out the live stream at https://www.twitch.tv/officialyugiohchannel!

At each YCS, Public Event players are given the opportunity to win the current YCS prize card,

! Four players are selected at random, and play to see who wins it. Four more players are selected based on the points they accumulated playing in Public Events. For YCS Origins, we have a third prize card to give away, four Duelists were chosen at random, but only from those who had gotten a five day badge for the Origins Game Fair. Here are the public event winners!
Shunping Xu won his Minerva in the points playoff!
Corey Shehl overcame three other random Duelists to take home his prize card!
Finally, Christian Urena had a five day Origins badge, and that’s letting him take home a Minerva!
Congratulations to all our Public Events prize card winners!

QQ stands for Quick Questions! We asked our YCS Origins Duelists what their favorite kind of monster is: Fusion, Ritual, Synchro, Xyz, or Pendulum; also, what was their favorite Deck using that strategy.
“Ritual monsters are my favorite kind of monsters. My favorite Deck involving them is Nekroz because of the versatility of how they interact from the hand.” – Andrew Tropp, 18
“Fusion. Don’t call me Fusion! Lunalights” – Casey Campbell, 29
“Synchro / Stardust Assault Mode Turbo” – Earl Boone, 35
There were also quite a few Duelists who liked Pendulum Monsters, but didn’t list a specific favorite Deck using them.

With that, we actually have quite an even split between all the answers of Rituals, Synchros, Xyz, and Pendulums. Not too many said Fusion (Maybe all the HERO Duelists stayed home?), but even that had several answers too.

A new Public Event is starting up here at YCS Origins, the Generation Duel! Entering this event lets you choose a generation of Yu-Gi-Oh! and build a Deck that embodies the spirit of an era of Dueling. If you win, you’ll get a unique game mat featuring the main characters from that period!
Each era has its own Forbidden & Limited List.

For the Classic Yu-Gi-Oh! era, you have access to all kinds of incredibly powerful cards that are normally Forbidden! In addition, you get to use most of those cards with their original text, rather than the recent text changes many of them received. That means you can use cards like
The GX era is all about Fusion Summons, thanks to Jaden’s HERO monsters.
In the 5D’s era, Synchro Summons reign supreme! Even the mighty

r.b: Brionac, Dragon of the Ice Barrier

r: can be played in this format!
Zexal introduced us to the Xyz Monsters, and they show their true power here!
And finally, the Arc-V era represents the current generation of Duelists, and uses the standard Advanced Format list.
The Generation Duel tournament is the ultimate way to pit the old against the new! For the full rules, including each era’s Forbidden & Limited List, click here.
